Particulates will be released during the removal or destruction of old plaster, brick veneer and exterior stucco surfaces and during the transport of these materials to disposal sites. This will occur both during some housing rehavilitations and more significantly during demolitions. Dust will also be raised by the operation of heavy equipment during the demolition of structures, the grading and preparation of sites, and during the construction of new sewer lines and street reconstruction and re-surfacing. Traffic related to these latter construction activities and the local resident traffic on temporarily unsurfaced streets will also contribute minor amounts of dust.
Since slightly over 25% of the time, the San Jose prevailing wind is from a northwesterly direction, the greatest particulate impact will be felt on the leeward, or southeasterly, side of the affected streets. The following mitigation measures are suggested to reduce the dust impact:
 Continuous water spraying of structures while demolition is in progress.
Wetting of exposed earth surfaces crossed by heavy equipment.
 Prompt removal of debris piles from reconstruction and demolition sites.
Wetting and covering of debris loads carried through neighborhoods.
Prompt revegetation of areas stripped by demolition.
Minimizing vehicle traffic and handling of dry materials on site.
 Performing dust-producing activities during the wetter, less windy months of the year (November to April).
The Mayfair neighborhood experiences relatively higher concentrations of carbon monoxide (CO) along the southerly and easterly boundary due to the proximity of Route 680. Possible mitigation measures in this vicinity would include weather stripping doors and windows and recirculation-type neating systems.
